messages.subject: Executive Value Proposition | PIF 2026-2030 | International Relations, ESG & Strategic Partnerships
messages.body:
Dear Mr. Trefgarne,

I am writing to share a strategic value brief prepared specifically for the Public Investment Fund as PIF moves into its 2026-2030 phase of value realization, investment efficiency, private-sector participation and global partnership building.

I currently serve as Liaison Director, Social Responsibility Department, at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group. My work sits at the intersection of senior government and regulatory relations, ESG, corporate affairs, strategic partnerships, stakeholder strategy and executive advisory within a capital-intensive, highly regulated operating environment. I coordinate complex matters across public institutions, technical teams, operations and senior management, translating external expectations into accountable execution.

My experience also includes stakeholder governance around a major solar and battery-storage platform, carbon-data traceability, regulatory coordination, social performance, local procurement and workforce-development interfaces. This gives me a practical operating perspective on the issues that arise when investment strategy meets government, regulation, communities and delivery.

Rather than send a conventional CV alone, I have attached a PIF-specific strategic value brief. It sets out where I believe my experience could support PIF or selected portfolio companies, together with a 90-180 day action framework and my three-page executive CV.

I would value a confidential discussion if you see alignment within PIF, its portfolio ecosystem, or leadership mandates spanning International Relations, Corporate Affairs, Sustainability and Stewardship, National Development, Strategic Partnerships or country-facing execution.

Kind regards,

Ragunauth Ramsaroop
Liaison Director | AGM Inc., Zijin Mining Group
Georgetown, Guyana
+592 608 4735

strategic_brief.title: Strategic Value Creation Proposition for PIF 2026-2030
strategic_brief.executive_summary: PIF's 2026-2030 strategy marks a shift toward deeper value realization, investment efficiency, private-sector participation and stronger integration across domestic ecosystems while preserving an international investment and partnership mandate. That next phase increases the importance of disciplined stakeholder execution across governments, regulators, portfolio companies, strategic partners and communities. My value proposition is to bring an operator's perspective to that interface. As Liaison Director at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group, I lead country-facing government and regulatory relations, ESG and social responsibility coordination, corporate affairs, stakeholder strategy and executive advisory in a capital-intensive mining environment. I would bring PIF a combination of institutional relationship management, regulated-market execution, ESG evidence discipline and cross-functional follow-through that is relevant to international partnerships, portfolio-company market entry, sustainability stewardship and country-level execution.
strategic_brief.company_context: PIF enters its 2026-2030 strategic phase from a position of significant scale. Its 2025 annual results reported more than US$900 billion in assets under management, US$120 billion in revenue, US$17 billion in net profit, more than US$199 billion in cumulative domestic investment since 2021 and more than US$342 billion contributed to Saudi Arabia's real non-oil GDP between 2021 and 2025. The new strategy places greater emphasis on competitive domestic ecosystems, long-term returns, investment efficiency, private-sector participation, national champions and global economic partnerships. PIF's fourth Private Sector Forum in February 2026 brought together more than 10,000 private-sector participants, over 120 portfolio companies and 18 government entities, illustrating the operating complexity of its ecosystem. As PIF scales value creation across multiple sectors and geographies, international relations, stakeholder alignment, portfolio-company institutional readiness, sustainability evidence and disciplined execution become increasingly important to protecting investment outcomes and supporting durable partnerships.

opportunities.title: International Stakeholder Architecture
opportunities.rationale: PIF's global partnerships and portfolio-company expansion create repeated interfaces with ministries, regulators, investment agencies, diplomatic stakeholders and local institutions. Those interfaces influence market entry, investment confidence, regulatory timelines and long-term operating legitimacy. A structured stakeholder architecture across priority geographies would help convert relationships into an institutional capability rather than relying on transaction-by-transaction engagement, while giving executives clearer visibility of political, regulatory and reputation dependencies around major initiatives.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would map priority stakeholders, decision pathways, regulatory touchpoints and engagement ownership across selected markets, then establish concise executive briefs, escalation routes, relationship plans and evidence standards. My current role requires this same discipline across multiple public agencies and operating functions where timing, trust and accountability directly affect business continuity.

opportunities.title: Portfolio Market Entry Readiness
opportunities.rationale: PIF's portfolio contains national champions and new companies that increasingly pursue partnerships, investment and operating opportunities beyond Saudi Arabia. International growth requires more than commercial strategy. Portfolio companies need early visibility of permitting, public-sector expectations, local-content requirements, community issues, ESG obligations and institutional sensitivities so that expansion decisions reflect the full execution environment before capital and reputation are committed.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would develop a practical market-entry and country-readiness framework for selected portfolio companies, integrating government relations, ESG, regulatory requirements, stakeholder mapping, local-partner considerations and implementation risk. My experience converting external requirements into cross-functional action would support portfolio teams moving from opportunity identification into disciplined country execution.

opportunities.title: Sustainability Stewardship Execution
opportunities.rationale: PIF has embedded sustainability into its financing, stewardship and investment agenda, including green-finance reporting and portfolio-level expectations. The challenge at scale is consistent execution and evidence. Strong sustainability governance depends on operating data, accountable owners, credible stakeholder engagement and traceable follow-through across portfolio companies, especially in infrastructure, mining, energy, industrial and other regulated sectors where environmental and social performance directly affect project delivery.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would support selected stewardship and portfolio workstreams by linking ESG commitments to operational evidence, stakeholder governance, action ownership and executive reporting. I have coordinated carbon-data traceability using physical operating records and supported stakeholder governance around approximately 46-50 MWp of solar capacity and more than 80 MWh of battery storage in a live mining environment.

opportunities.title: Mining Energy Partnership Bridge
opportunities.rationale: Saudi Arabia is expanding mining, minerals, renewable energy, industrial capacity and supply-chain localization as connected growth engines. PIF's ecosystem touches these sectors through national champions, infrastructure platforms and strategic partnerships. International mining and energy projects often require alignment among investors, governments, regulators, communities, contractors and technical operators, creating a need for leaders who understand both institutional expectations and the realities of operating assets.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would bring direct mining-sector operating exposure, government and regulatory coordination, renewable-energy stakeholder experience and multinational group experience to partnership or portfolio-company mandates connected to minerals, energy transition and industrial development. My role has required translating policy and stakeholder expectations into actions that technical and corporate teams can execute and evidence.

opportunities.title: Executive Issues and Reputation Readiness
opportunities.rationale: At PIF's scale, portfolio activity, international partnerships and high-profile projects generate issues where operational facts, stakeholder expectations and public positioning need to remain aligned. Fast executive decisions depend on concise evidence, clear ownership and disciplined escalation. A repeatable issues-management approach across selected high-exposure workstreams would strengthen response quality while helping prevent communication or stakeholder gaps from becoming investment, regulatory or reputation problems.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would establish concise executive decision briefs, stakeholder-risk registers, action trackers and escalation protocols for priority matters. I routinely coordinate reputation-sensitive, regulator-facing and cross-functional issues involving operations, HSE, environment, legal, finance, procurement, HR, security and senior management, with emphasis on accuracy, ownership and closure.

days_0_30: Confirm the PIF division, portfolio-company set or international markets where government, stakeholder, ESG or country-execution support would create the strongest near-term value.
Map priority ministries, regulators, investment agencies, strategic partners, community interfaces and internal owners against live strategic objectives and existing relationship coverage.
Review current executive reporting, stakeholder intelligence, ESG evidence and escalation processes to identify duplication, gaps and decision bottlenecks.
days_31_60: Select three to five priority pilots based on strategic value, execution risk and leadership sponsorship.
Build integrated stakeholder and country-readiness plans with clear objectives, ownership, engagement cadence, evidence requirements and escalation thresholds.
Create an executive dashboard covering institutional dependencies, commitments, emerging risks, partnership opportunities and delivery status.
days_61_90: Launch pilot engagement plans with agreed internal owners and concise briefing materials for senior leadership.
Embed ESG and stakeholder evidence into priority project or portfolio reviews so external commitments connect to operating data and accountable actions.
Establish a structured lessons process to identify repeatable practices across portfolio companies and markets.
days_91_180: Scale the strongest pilot practices into a common toolkit for international stakeholder strategy, country readiness and portfolio-company execution.
Measure impact through decision-cycle time, issue closure, stakeholder outcomes, evidence quality, partnership progress and avoided execution friction.
Institutionalize a reporting cadence that gives leadership early visibility of cross-border opportunities, regulatory dependencies and reputation-sensitive matters.

potential_impact: Earlier visibility of government, regulatory and stakeholder dependencies before they become transaction or project delays.
Stronger portfolio-company readiness for international market entry and country-level execution.
More consistent translation of ESG and stewardship commitments into operating evidence, action ownership and executive reporting.
Higher-quality executive decisions through concise stakeholder intelligence, issue escalation and cross-functional accountability.
A repeatable institutional framework connecting international relations, portfolio strategy and on-the-ground execution across priority markets.
background_relevance: Current Liaison Director at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group, with country-facing responsibility spanning government and regulatory relations, ESG, social responsibility, corporate affairs, stakeholder strategy and executive communications.
Leads senior institutional engagement across mining, environment, energy, aviation, labour, standards, taxation, trade, investment and social-performance matters in a regulated operating environment.

Coordinates inspections, permits, commitments, official visits and sensitive external matters across operations, HSE, environment, legal, HR, finance, procurement, security, aviation and technical teams.
Supports stakeholder governance around approximately 46-50 MWp of solar capacity and more than 80 MWh of battery storage, connecting climate objectives with operating and institutional requirements.

Coordinated a 2026 carbon-accounting proof of concept linking physical operating records across fuel, electricity, explosives, material movement, production and refinery data to strengthen traceability and review readiness.
Brings 12+ years across multinational mining, regulated financial services and commercial operations, plus an MBA and international executive-development exposure.
